title: A negative-count threshold is linear
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the coordinates, and let $k$ be a natural number. Define a sign-valued gate to output $-1$ when at least $k$ coordinates in $S$ are positive, and $1$ otherwise. This gate is a linear threshold function: there are real weights and a real offset such that its value at each sign vector is the sign of the resulting affine linear form.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a subset of the coordinates
